note: Curated drug-target complexes selected from experimentally determined structures. Each entry declares a category (viral, human_enzyme, human_receptor) and a tier: 'curated' entries carry a mechanism narrative whose statements are tagged LITERATURE and backed by a fetched citation (title, DOI/PMID), while 'contacts_only' entries carry no narrative at all. Ligand codes, titles, organisms and resolutions were read from the RCSB entry metadata, not from memory. Interaction values are computed at request time from the deposited coordinates. Catalytic-residue identities are literature facts and are labelled as such; the statement that a given residue is (or is not) in contact is measured.

complexes.protein_title: Crystal structure at 1.9 A resolution of HIV II protease complexed with L-735,524 (indinavir)
complexes.mechanism_summary: HIV-1 protease is a homodimeric aspartic protease that cleaves the viral Gag-Pol polyprotein into the mature structural and enzymatic proteins the virus needs to become infectious. Indinavir is a peptidomimetic inhibitor shaped like the substrate transition state, so it binds the same active site the polyprotein would occupy.
complexes.consequence: Because the polyprotein is never cleaved, the virus assembles non-infectious, immature virions. This is why HIV protease inhibitors must be present continuously: they block a step of maturation, not the production of viral RNA.
sources: PDB entry 1HSG - Chen et al., J. Biol. Chem. 1994, 'Crystal structure at 1.9 A resolution of HIV II protease complexed with L-735,524'

complexes.protein_title: High resolution structures of HIV-1 RT from four RT-inhibitor complexes
complexes.target_class: Viral RNA-dependent DNA polymerase (HIV-1 reverse transcriptase)
complexes.mechanism_summary: Reverse transcriptase copies the viral RNA genome into DNA, which the virus then inserts into the host chromosome. Nevirapine is a non-nucleoside inhibitor: it does not look like a nucleotide and does not bind the polymerase active site. It occupies a hydrophobic allosteric pocket in the p66 subunit roughly 10 A from the catalytic residues and locks the enzyme in an inactive conformation.
complexes.consequence: With the enzyme held in that inactive shape, viral RNA is never copied into DNA and the replication cycle stops before integration. Because the site is allosteric rather than catalytic, a single point mutation in the pocket (for example K103N or Y181C) is often enough to abolish binding, which is why NNRTI resistance emerges readily.

complexes.display_name: Influenza A neuraminidase with Oseltamivir carboxylate
complexes.protein_title: N1 neuraminidase in complex with oseltamivir
complexes.target_class: Viral sialidase (influenza A neuraminidase, N1 subtype)
complexes.mechanism_summary: Neuraminidase is the influenza enzyme that clips sialic acid residues off the surface of the infected cell and off newly budded virions. That clipping is what releases progeny virions so they can spread. Oseltamivir carboxylate is a transition-state analogue: its cyclohexene scaffold and carboxylate present the same features the enzyme recognises in its sialic-acid substrate, so it binds the catalytic site.
complexes.consequence: New virions stay tethered to the infected cell and clump together instead of spreading, so the infection does not amplify efficiently. The enzyme is blocked, not the virus's entry or its genome copying.
sources: PDB entry 2HU4 - Russell et al., Nature 2006, 'The structure of H5N1 avian influenza neuraminidase suggests new opportunities for drug design'

complexes.display_name: Human angiotensin-converting enzyme with Lisinopril (human enzyme example, not a virus)
complexes.protein_title: Crystal structure of human angiotensin converting enzyme in complex with lisinopril
complexes.mechanism_summary: Angiotensin-converting enzyme is a human zinc metallopeptidase that converts angiotensin I into the vasoconstrictor angiotensin II and degrades bradykinin. Lisinopril carries a carboxylate that coordinates the catalytic zinc ion and occupies the substrate-binding channel.
complexes.consequence: With the enzyme blocked, angiotensin II production falls and bradykinin is preserved, which lowers blood pressure. This is a human drug target, included as an example of the same method applied to a non-viral enzyme. The structure also contains a zinc ion, chloride ions and a glycated lysine, all of which are excluded from the ligand analysis because they are not the drug.
sources: PDB entry 1O86 - Natesh et al., Nature 2003, 'Crystal structure of the human angiotensin-converting enzyme-lisinopril complex'

complexes.display_name: Human EGFR kinase domain with Erlotinib
complexes.protein_title: Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor tyrosine kinase domain with 4-anilinoquinazoline inhibitor erlotinib
complexes.target_class: Human receptor tyrosine kinase (epidermal growth factor receptor, kinase domain)
complexes.mechanism_summary: The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is a receptor tyrosine kinase whose kinase domain is active without a phosphorylation event, which the authors note distinguishes the EGFR family from other receptor tyrosine kinases. The deposited structure is the EGFR kinase domain, including forty residues of the carboxyl-terminal tail, determined both with and without the 4-anilinoquinazoline inhibitor erlotinib (OSI-774, CP-358,774) at 2.6 A.
complexes.consequence: Erlotinib occupies the kinase domain that carries out the receptor's own phosphorylation. The paper describes erlotinib as an EGFR-specific anti-cancer agent that was in Phase III clinical trials when the structure was determined, and discusses carboxyl-terminal tail contacts in relation to receptor oligomerisation.

complexes.display_name: Human Abl kinase domain with Imatinib
complexes.protein_title: Human Abl kinase domain in complex with imatinib (STI571, Glivec)
complexes.target_class: Human non-receptor tyrosine kinase (Abl kinase domain)
complexes.mechanism_summary: Chronic myelogenous leukaemia results from the Bcr-Abl oncoprotein, whose Abl tyrosine kinase domain is constitutively activated. Imatinib (STI571, Glivec) is an Abl kinase inhibitor, and the deposited structure is the human Abl kinase domain in complex with it at 2.4 A.
complexes.consequence: The authors report that most chronic-phase CML patients treated with imatinib as first-line therapy maintain durable responses, while patients who progressed to advanced-stage disease frequently fail to respond or lose their response through drug-resistant Abl mutants, of which more than 40 point mutations had been observed. The structures were determined to understand that resistance and to support inhibitor design.

citations.title: Structural biology contributions to the discovery of drugs to treat chronic myelogenous leukaemia
citations.authors: Cowan-Jacob SW, Fendrich G, Floersheimer A, et al.

complexes.protein_title: Human estrogen receptor alpha ligand-binding domain in complex with 4-hydroxytamoxifen
complexes.target_class: Human nuclear receptor (estrogen receptor alpha, ligand-binding domain)
complexes.mechanism_summary: Estrogen receptor alpha is a nuclear receptor whose ligand-dependent activation of transcription is mediated by interactions with coactivators. The deposited structure is the human estrogen receptor alpha ligand-binding domain bound to the antagonist 4-hydroxytamoxifen (OHT).
complexes.consequence: In the OHT complex, helix 12 occludes the coactivator-recognition groove by mimicking the interactions of the coactivator NR-box peptide, which is how the antagonist blocks coactivator binding. The authors describe this as an autoinhibitory helix-12 conformation and identify two distinct structural mechanisms by which OHT promotes it.

complexes.protein_title: Crystal Structure of Recombinant Human Acetylcholinesterase in Complex with Donepezil
complexes.mechanism_summary: Human acetylcholinesterase is described by the authors as a significant target for therapeutic drugs. The deposited structure is human acetylcholinesterase in complex with donepezil, an Alzheimer's disease drug; the paper reports that donepezil binds human acetylcholinesterase differently from the Torpedo enzyme.
complexes.consequence: The authors present these structures of the human enzyme as a more accurate platform for drug development than the previously available ones, precisely because the human and Torpedo enzymes bind donepezil differently. The abstract does not quantify a clinical effect, so none is claimed here.

complexes.protein_title: Crystal structure of PDE5 in complex with sildenafil

catalytic_residues.label: Gly659
catalytic_residues.role: Invariant glycine immediately preceding the H-loop; the authors report it is critical for optimal substrate affinity and catalytic activity

complexes.mechanism_summary: Phosphodiesterase-5 (PDE5) is the target of sildenafil, vardenafil and tadalafil, drugs used to treat erectile dysfunction and pulmonary hypertension. The deposited structure is a fully active catalytic domain of PDE5A1 in complex with sildenafil.
complexes.consequence: Inhibitor binding reorganises the active-site H-loop (residues 660-683), which has four different conformations across the reported structures and migrates 7-35 A. The authors' mutagenesis and kinetic analyses identify the H-loop as important for substrate recognition.

complexes.display_name: Human carbonic anhydrase II with Acetazolamide
complexes.protein_title: Human carbonic anhydrase II complexed with acetazolamide
complexes.mechanism_summary: The deposited structure is human carbonic anhydrase II in complex with the sulfonamide inhibitor acetazolamide (AZM), determined at 1.1 A. The authors report that AZM binds directly to the zinc and makes several key interactions with active-site residues.
complexes.consequence: Because AZM binds directly to the zinc, the active site is occupied at the metal itself. The same high-resolution structure showed a glycerol molecule adjacent to AZM in the active site and two additional AZM molecules adventitiously bound on the enzyme surface, which the authors discuss in relation to isozyme-specific inhibitor design.

citations.title: High-resolution structure of human carbonic anhydrase II complexed with acetazolamide reveals insights into inhibitor drug design

complexes.protein_title: Complex of the catalytic portion of human HMG-CoA reductase with atorvastatin
complexes.mechanism_summary: HMG-CoA reductase catalyses the committed step in cholesterol biosynthesis, and statins inhibit it with inhibition constants in the nanomolar range. The deposited structure is the catalytic portion of human HMG-CoA reductase in complex with atorvastatin.
complexes.consequence: The statins occupy a portion of the HMG-CoA binding site and so block access of the substrate to the active site, which is a competitive mechanism rather than binding elsewhere on the enzyme. The authors also report that several catalytically relevant residues near the carboxyl terminus are disordered in the enzyme-statin complexes and would sterically hinder statin binding if they were not flexible.

citations.title: Structural mechanism for statin inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase

sources: Istvan ES, Deisenhofer J. Structural mechanism for statin inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase Science 2001. DOI 10.1126/science.1059344; PMID 11349148
